hosting.comment: ORDER MATTERS, AND IT IS LAST-MATCH-WINS. This is the opposite of `rewrites`, where the FIRST matching rule applies, and it is not stated in the docs — it was established by deploying and reading the live headers. So the broad catch-all goes FIRST and the specific immutable rules go LAST; putting `**` at the end silently flattened every asset to no-cache.

headers.comment: Every navigation URL. no-cache means 'revalidate before use', NOT 'do not store' — an unchanged file still costs only a 304, but a new deploy is picked up on the very next visit instead of up to an hour later, which is what makes the service worker's update banner appear promptly. A literal '/index.html' source does NOT work: the SPA rewrite serves '/' and '/configure' from index.html without their request paths ever being '/index.html', so those responses kept Firebase's default max-age=3600. Overridden below for hashed assets.
Vite stamps a content hash into every filename under /assets, so a given URL can never change contents. Cache for a year and skip revalidation entirely.
Fonts are versioned by hand but are equally immutable in practice.
